method: Conservative per-ayah screening of Quran 2:201–210 and direct inspection of original-language Hebrew/Aramaic alongside accessible translations for candidates; this is preliminary, not comprehensive primary-source verification. No absence claim is exhaustive.

Divine coming in cloud shadows accompanied by angels and final adjudication; staged comparison with Sinai cloud theophany (Exod 19:9–11); Daniel 7:13 cloud vision is a contrasting second candidate, not an identical agent or event.

candidates.reading: Mechon-Mamre Hebrew-English Exodus 19:9–11; original Hebrew and translation inspected, no critical manuscript collation
candidates.shared: Divine coming or manifestation associated with cloud imagery.
candidates.difference: Exodus is Sinai revelation to Moses and Israel with a stated third-day appearance; Qur'an 2:210 concerns anticipated divine coming with angels and the settling of matters.
candidates.limits: Not a shared narrated event; edition-specific manuscript witnesses, literary formation, and dependence remain unestablished.

candidates.reading: Sefaria Aramaic and English Daniel 7:13–14 inspected; critical edition and witness comparison pending
candidates.shared: Heavenly cloud imagery in an eschatological or royal-judgment setting.
candidates.difference: Daniel depicts one like a human being arriving with heaven's clouds before the Ancient of Days and receiving dominion; Qur'an depicts God's coming in cloud shadows with angels and the matter decided.
candidates.limits: Different actors, movement and literary genre; do not identify the Danielic figure with God or infer borrowing.
